title: approve-enrollment
description: Approve a pending cabinet: where it belongs, what it is called, its role, and the baseline it is judged against. A satellite may name the sync cabinet it reaches (an active sync cabinet at the same site); left out, it is linked to the site's only sync cabinet, or stays incomplete until one is assigned. Every approval carries a baseline decision. It may name the cabinet it replaces.

syncCabinetId.description: The sync cabinet this satellite reaches. Only a satellite names one.

replacesCabinetId.description: The active cabinet this one replaces (a failed drive, a reinstalled agent): a cabinet at the same client and site, with the same role. The old cabinet is retired with its history kept, and this one takes its name, its sync link and its own settings (docs/spec/05-server-spec.md "Replacing a cabinet").

scanner.description: For a new client only: whether it uses a fingerprint scanner, with its service when it does. An existing client keeps its own setting, so the approval refuses this field for one (change it on the client's page).

sitePolicies.description: For a new site only: its own firewall policy and time zone, pre-filled by the console from what it would inherit and confirmed by the approver. An existing site keeps its own settings, so the approval refuses this field for one (change them on the site's page).

baseline.description: The baseline decision every approval needs (docs/spec/15-baselines-and-config.md "Baselines at enrollment"). inherited: an approved baseline already applies (fleet, role, client or site level), and the server checks that one does. attach: copy the named approved baseline version to the cabinet's site as the site's baseline. capture: the cabinet's first full configuration report becomes the site's baseline draft, which is then reviewed and approved with the two-person rule.

stepUpToken.description: A one-time step-up token bound to this exact action.

not.description: Only a satellite reaches a sync cabinet. Refusing the field on another role is clearer than ignoring it.
